builder_plan.scenario: Start with one repeated product task that has a measurable failure or cost.
builder_plan.change: Read the methods and identify one change you can isolate in that workflow.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current implementation on the same held-out tasks.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Successful outcomes, response time, human rework, and total cost per successful task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Block-Sparse Gauss-Newton Optimization of Finite Basis Physics-Informed Neural Networks: Sparse Automatic Differentiation Approach
summary: The method replaces first-order optimizers (e.g., Adam) for training finite-basis physics-informed neural networks with a Gauss-Newton scheme that exploits domain-decomposition-induced block sparsity, using graph coloring to compress Jacobian computation and sparse direct or preconditioned iterative solvers for the Gauss-Newton system. It costs substantial implementation complexity: sparse automatic differentiation infrastructure, graph coloring of Jacobian structure, and sparse linear algebra tooling, none of which are standard components in typical ML stacks. It can fail when the PDE residual problem does not decompose into overlapping subdomains with localized subnetwork influence, when the Gauss-Newton approximation is poor (e.g., far from convergence or non-least-squares structure), or when the problem size is small enough that second-order overhead exceeds any convergence benefit.
rationale: This technique is specific to scientific machine learning on PDE-constrained problems and has no bearing on LLM inference, serving, or agent workloads on a single 24 GB GPU.
